page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz, the x86_64 processor includes a 50 MB L3 cache and supports hardware extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, AES cryptography, and FMA. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It also includes 131 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between processing power and memory capabilities. The CPU performance is generally modest, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core benchmarks, placing in the bottom 25% tier. However, the memory subsystem performance is more robust, with memory bandwidth read and write tests scoring in the average range (middle 50%), including a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 365.1 GB/sec. Passmark CPU, memory, and database operations also register average performance tiers.

From a resource density perspective, the E8s_v3 offers high memory capacity relative to its compute resources, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU throughput. Tradeoffs include weaker performance in compute-heavy tasks, such as image processing, text processing, and static web serving, which all fall into the bottom 25% tier. LLM text generation with a 7B model is poor, scoring in the bottom 10%. Consequently, this server is best suited for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, caching layers, and moderate database operations rather than high-performance computing or large-scale AI inference.
